target_name: Two Year Soft Asset Bloat Within Cheap Firms
rationale: This is pure horizon interpolation between two already-tested variants (1-year and 3-year) of the same gated bloat signal — a cosmetic parameter tweak with no new economic content, and the "interior optimum" framing is post-hoc metric-shopping rather than a mechanism test.

target_name: Working Capital Bloat Excluding Intangibles Within Cheap Firms
rationale: Excising intangibles is a genuine attribution test that decomposes the winning discriminator into economically distinct channels and is internally consistent in sign, though the reviewer should note the resulting measure sits very close to balance-sheet operating accruals (Sloan) and its documented value/glamour interaction, so a positive result must be benchmarked against plain accruals rather than claimed as new.

target_name: Demand Validated Soft Asset Bloat Within Cheap Firms
rationale: Benchmarking soft-asset growth against revenue rather than total assets is a substantively different scaling choice with a clear diagnosis of why the EBITDA-benchmarked version failed in the cheap tail, and the NEG-wrapped expression matches the stated positive expected sign.

target_name: Cash Yield Gated Soft Asset Bloat
rationale: Swapping the book-based gate for a cash-flow-yield gate is a legitimate test of whether the conditioning set or the specific value proxy drives the alpha, but it is a gate substitution rather than a new mechanism, and the oancf-based gate will materially cut coverage (~0.09 elsewhere in the archive), so any apparent improvement must be checked against sparsity.

target_name: Total Expansion Breadth Within Cheap Firms
rationale: The hypothesis claims discipline must be *simultaneous* on both fronts, but an additive z-score composite lets extreme restraint on one dimension fully offset expansion on the other — a conjunction claim requires MIN or a double-sort, so the expression does not compute what the stated economics assert, and as written it is a straightforward ensemble of two already-validated components.

target_name: Soft Asset Bloat Across Both Valuation Tails
rationale: The sign logic is correct (bloat predicts underperformance in both tails, so a single NEG-wrapped discriminator reinforces rather than cancels) and the contrast with the failed reinvestment two-tail design is well argued, but it reuses an existing archive template and, if it works, mostly indicates the conditioning is doing little — i.e., it collapses toward the unconditional asset-growth/net-operating-asset anomaly, which must be controlled for.
